note: Built as ballot/lean/mn_endorsements.json is. Each record is one line of one party page, matched to one race and one candidate on the official lists already loaded in ballot_local_2026.sqlite (office, place and name all fit, one fit only). Michigan differs from Minnesota: parties nominate for the Legislature and for governor in the August 4 primary, and nominate the secretary of state, the attorney general, the education boards and the Supreme Court justices at conventions; the justices are then printed with no party. Both major parties held early 'endorsement conventions' (Republicans March 28, Democrats April 19, 2026). Only a page that itself says 'endorse' or 'endorsed' is under endorsements. A voter guide, a slate, a list of the party's candidates or a 'recommended' column is under other_support with the page's own word in 'kind', kept apart and not for showing as an endorsement; from a bare list of a party's candidates only the offices printed without a party (judges, school boards) are taken, since the rest adds nothing to the party on the ballot. Governor and lieutenant governor are one November ticket, so a page's two lines are one record. 'election' appears only when the candidate is on a primary list and not on the November list. Federal offices, ballot proposals and party offices on these pages are outside this file. The same candidate stands on several lists: count once per party. Names are spelled as our record spells them; 'as_listed' keeps the page's spelling. Pages were fetched with the kit's honest User-Agent after checking each site's robots.txt; a site that forbids programs, shows a challenge or refuses the program was not opened (see not_read). The Oakland County Republican slate is drawn by a script: its names and its heading 'GOP-endorsed candidates' (county courts and school boards only) were read from that script, and nothing else in it was read. Every page in 'lists' was opened again when this file was built and a record is kept only if the page still showed the name. County and local races are loaded for nine counties only (Wayne, Oakland, Macomb, Kent, Ottawa, Ingham, Kalamazoo, Saginaw, Muskegon), so lines for other places (Washtenaw's cities and school boards, Jackson's) cannot match yet; they are listed under the two 'unmatched_listed' keys with the reason.
